sentences.text:
Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pramod Kumar Agrawal
 On The 3 rd Of December, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 52629 of 2025
 Ravi Balmik
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Prakhar Naveriya - Advocate for applicant.
Smt. Ranjana Agnihotri - Dy. Ga for State.

Order 
This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of the BNSS, 2023/439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.182/2023 registered at Police Station Batkakhapa, District Chhindwara (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366(1), 376(2)
(n), 376(3) and 34 of the IPC and Sections 3/4, 5/6 of POCSO Act, 2012.

Applicant is in detention since 26.05.2025.
2.
As per the prosecution story, on 11.09.2023, father of prosecutrix lodged a report alleging that his daughter was missing at P.S. Batkakhapa, District Chhindwara.
The police registered the initial offence under Section 363 of IPC against the unknown person and investigated the matter.
During investigation, police recovered the prosecutrix along with applicant.
The statement of prosecutrix was recorded and then police added additional offences against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is in jail since 26.05.2025.
Applicant is i n n o c e n t a n d h e h a s b e e n f a l s e l y i m p l i c a t e d . I t i s N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2025:MPHC-JBP:62890 2 MCRC-52629-2025 submitted that proseuctrix in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. has not deposed against the present applicant.
Co-accused Sanju has been enlarged on bail by this Court on 28.08.2028.
The charge-sheet has been filed in the present case.
The learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that the FIR was lodged with inordinate delay.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant.

sentences.text: Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merit of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Consequently, bail application under Section 483 of the BNSS, 2023/439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of the BNSS.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:62890 3 MCRC-52629-2025 Sateesh Ravi Balmik vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45592155/
